distance.locator: KEK K2K FAQ page, answer on the beam path
distance.note: The K2K paper states it twice: "uses an accelerator-produced beam of nearly pure νμ with a neutrino flight distance of 250 km" (§I) and the far detector "which is located 250 km away from KEK" (§III). The KEK end is site:kek-tsukuba-belle-ii, the only KEK site in the Atlas (the KEK Tsukuba campus, used as a proxy: the Atlas has no record for the KEK-PS neutrino beamline site itself). The great-circle distance between the two recorded points is 249.6 km (0.2 % from the stated value).
distance.quote: After passing through the near detectors, the neutrino beam enters the earth and emerges at Super-Kamiokande, 250 km away.

direction.quote: the neutrino beam enters the earth and emerges at Super-Kamiokande, 250 km away.
direction.value: Bent from the North hall towards Kamioka and into the earth, emerging at Super-Kamiokande 250 km away

intervals.label: commissioning
intervals.note: The KEK K2K page (written before the event) says the beam commissioning "is scheduled in January, 1999"; physics data taking began in June 1999 per the K2K measurement paper. No source read confirms the actual commissioning month.
intervals.quote: The commissioning of the neutrino beam is scheduled in January, 1999.

intervals.label: end of operation
intervals.note: K2K data taking ended in November 2004; the KEK-PS itself ran until December 2005.

secondary_beam.quote: a high intensity muon neutrino beam with average evergy of 1.5 GeV, produced at KEK-PS
secondary_beam.value: Muon neutrinos, on-axis, mean energy about 1.5 GeV

baseline.note: Also recorded as a site-to-site baseline in `baselines` (KEK Tsukuba campus point to Super-Kamiokande).
baseline.quote: a neutrino flight distance of 250 km

summary.plain: The beamline at KEK that made the world's first accelerator neutrino beam aimed at a detector hundreds of kilometres away: 12 GeV protons on an aluminium rod, two magnetic horns, and a 200-metre pipe in which the particles decayed into neutrinos.
summary.technical: Single-turn extracted 12 GeV protons from the KEK-PS onto a 66 cm long, 3 cm diameter aluminium target inside a two-horn focusing system, followed by a 200 m decay volume and a beam dump; near detectors at about 300 m, Super-Kamiokande at 250 km. Mean neutrino energy about 1.5 GeV.

target.note: The K2K measurement paper records that the target diameter was increased from 2 cm to 3 cm in November 1999.
target.quote: aluminum rod of 66 cm in length and 3 cm in diameter
target.value: Aluminium rod, 66 cm long and 3 cm in diameter, inside the first of two focusing horns
